issues.title: Bug: Expand ErrorLog.HttpResponseMessage field — currently truncated to 25 characters
issues.description:
## Summary
The `ErrorLog` entity (`OneNListApp.Data/Models/ErrorLog.cs`) stores the HTTP
response message in a field truncated to 25 characters. This means administrators
viewing the error log see messages like `"An error occurred while"` with no
indication of what the full error was. Full error context is lost and debugging
requires searching application logs by timestamp, which may not be retained.

**Affected file:** `Source/OneNListApp.Data/Models/ErrorLog.cs`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The `HttpResponseMessage` column in `ErrorLog` is expanded to at minimum 2000 characters (or `nvarchar(max)`)
- [ ] A database migration is created to alter the column length
- [ ] The corresponding EF Core model property is updated (remove or increase `[MaxLength]` attribute)
- [ ] Existing error logging calls that truncated input are updated to pass the full message
- [ ] The Admin error log view displays the full message (with a truncated preview in the list and full text on detail/expand)
- [ ] The `ErrorLog_Archive` table receives the same column length update
- [ ] All existing tests that reference `ErrorLog` continue to pass

issues.title: Bug: Fix blocking .Result calls on async methods in BulkUploadController
issues.description:
## Summary
`BulkUploadController` calls `.Result` on async methods at lines 107 and 140,
synchronously blocking the thread while waiting for database or service operations.
Under concurrent load this causes ASP.NET thread pool starvation — all available
threads block waiting for I/O, new requests queue up, and the server becomes
unresponsive. This is a known anti-pattern in ASP.NET Core.

**Affected file:** `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Controllers/BulkUploadController.cs:107,140`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All `.Result` and `.Wait()` calls in `BulkUploadController` are replaced with `await`
- [ ] The controller actions that perform these operations are converted to `async Task<IActionResult>`
- [ ] A search of all Web and API controllers is performed for other `.Result`/`.Wait()` usages; each found is converted or documented with a reason for the synchronous call
- [ ] All existing bulk upload controller unit tests pass after the conversion
- [ ] No deadlock occurs under a simple load test (10 concurrent uploads)

issues.title: Performance: Disable global lazy-loading and add explicit .Include() calls to fix N+1 queries
issues.description:
## Summary
`OneNListContext` enables EF Core lazy-loading proxies globally
(`optionsBuilder.UseLazyLoadingProxies()`, line 20). The `OneNList` entity has
290+ properties and many navigation properties (lookups, history records,
post-award records). Each navigation access triggers a separate database query,
creating N+1 query problems. A list page loading 50 action items can generate
thousands of individual SQL queries, causing significant performance degradation
as data grows.

**Affected file:** `Source/OneNListApp.Data/OneNListContext.cs:20`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `UseLazyLoadingProxies()` is removed from `OneNListContext`
- [ ] All existing queries that relied on lazy-loading are audited and updated with explicit `.Include()` / `.ThenInclude()` calls for the navigation properties they access
- [ ] A SQL query count test (or EF Core logging) confirms that common list/detail page loads execute ≤ 5 queries instead of N+50
- [ ] No `NullReferenceException` or missing-data regressions are introduced (navigation properties previously auto-loaded now return null without explicit Include)
- [ ] The stored procedure context (`OneNListStoredProcedureContext`) is unaffected
- [ ] All existing unit tests pass; integration tests (if any) pass against the actual database

issues.title: Security: Fix XSS vulnerability — replace innerHTML assignment in customAlerts.js
issues.description:
## Summary
`customAlerts.js` line 46 directly assigns user-supplied or server-supplied HTML
to `element.innerHTML`:

```js
element.innerHTML = html;
```

If any part of the `html` parameter originates from user input or an unsanitized
server response, this is a Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) sink. Although DOMPurify is
imported elsewhere in the codebase (`onenlist.modal.js`), it is not applied before
this assignment.

**Affected file:** `Source/OneNListApp.Web/wwwroot/scripts/customAlerts.js:46`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The direct `innerHTML` assignment on line 46 is replaced with `DOMPurify.sanitize(html)` before assignment, or with DOM API methods (`createElement`, `textContent`, `appendChild`) where plain text is sufficient
- [ ] All call sites of `custAlertModal` are audited; any that pass unsanitized server-rendered HTML are updated
- [ ] A Semgrep rule (`rules/xss-innerhtml.yaml`) is added to the repo to catch future direct `innerHTML` assignments without sanitization
- [ ] The custom alert modal continues to render correctly in all existing usages (error messages, confirmation dialogs)
- [ ] No regression in alert dialog functionality

issues.title: Security: Add CSRF anti-forgery token validation to BulkUpload POST action
issues.description:
## Summary
The `BulkUploadController.Upload` POST action (line 119) is missing the
`[ValidateAntiForgeryToken]` attribute. All other state-changing POST actions in
the Web application include this attribute to prevent Cross-Site Request Forgery
attacks. The bulk upload endpoint is accessible to authenticated users and could be
abused by a malicious site to trigger a file upload on behalf of a logged-in user.

**Affected file:** `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Controllers/BulkUploadController.cs:119`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `[ValidateAntiForgeryToken]` is added to the `Upload` POST action in `BulkUploadController`
- [ ] The corresponding Razor view includes `@Html.AntiForgeryToken()` inside the upload form (verify it is already present or add it)
- [ ] A search of all POST actions across Web controllers confirms no other state-changing actions are missing the attribute; any found are fixed or documented with justification
- [ ] Existing bulk upload unit tests are updated to include a valid anti-forgery token in test requests, or the test setup mocks the validation
- [ ] The upload workflow functions correctly end-to-end after the fix

issues.title: Security: Implement API key expiration and rate limiting on API endpoints
issues.description:
## Summary
PULSE API keys (`ApiConfClient`) have a `DtExpires` column but `ApiKeyAuthAttribute`
does not enforce expiration — keys issued years ago remain valid indefinitely.
Additionally, there is no rate limiting on any API endpoint, meaning a single API
key can make unlimited requests per second, enabling accidental or intentional
resource exhaustion.

**Affected files:**
- `Source/OneNListApp.API/Helpers/ApiKeyAuthAttribute.cs`
- `Source/OneNListApp.Data/Models/ApiConfClient.cs`
- `Source/OneNListApp.API/Program.cs` or `Startup.cs`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `ApiKeyAuthAttribute` checks `DtExpires` against `DateTime.UtcNow`; expired keys receive HTTP 401 with message `"API key has expired. Contact your administrator to renew."`
- [ ] An ASP.NET Core rate-limiting middleware (e.g., `Microsoft.AspNetCore.RateLimiting`) is configured on the API project
- [ ] Default rate limit: 100 requests per minute per API key; limit is configurable via `appsettings.json`
- [ ] Rate-limited requests receive HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header
- [ ] Expiration enforcement is covered by at least 2 new unit tests in `AuthenticationTests.cs`
- [ ] Rate limiting is documented in `docs/api-reference` wiki page
- [ ] All existing authentication unit tests (260 total) continue to pass

issues.title: Security: Centralize multi-tenant org filtering to prevent cross-org data access
issues.description:
## Summary
PULSE uses soft multi-tenancy: each `OneNList` record has a `fk_OrganizationId`
column, and each query is expected to filter by the current user's organization.
However, there is no centralized enforcement of this filter — each service, controller,
and stored procedure must independently remember to apply the org filter. A missed
filter in any query would expose another organization's data to the requesting user.

This is a data isolation risk: a bug in any query can silently leak sensitive tenant data across
organizational boundaries.

**Affected file:** `Source/OneNListApp.Data/OneNListContext.cs`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] EF Core Global Query Filters (`modelBuilder.Entity<OneNList>().HasQueryFilter(...)`) are implemented for all multi-tenant entities to automatically apply the `fk_OrganizationId` filter
- [ ] The current organization ID is provided to the DbContext via a scoped `IOrganizationContext` service (injected from the session) rather than passed ad-hoc to each query
- [ ] A unit test confirms that a query executed with OrgId=1 cannot return records belonging to OrgId=2
- [ ] Stored procedures that perform cross-org queries (reports, analytics) are explicitly documented with a comment explaining why the global filter is bypassed, and are gated by `[CustomAuthorize(eAccessLevel.Admin)]`
- [ ] All existing service and controller unit tests pass after the refactor
- [ ] No regression in multi-org admin views that intentionally show data across organizations
